name: Magnetic energy density u = B^2/(2 mu_0)

source.located: Classical electrodynamics: Maxwell's field energy density (Maxwell 1865/1873; standard restatements Jackson Classical Electrodynamics sec. 6.7, Landau-Lifshitz vol. 2 sec. 31-33). Intended arXiv restatements for the vacuum-QED limit: Dunne, 'Heisenberg-Euler effective Lagrangians: basics and extensions', hep-th/0406216; CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787, for mu_0.

published_statement: NOT QUOTED FROM SOURCE (unread, see source.via). The statement as derived here from the Maxwell action: T_00 = (eps0 E^2 + B^2/mu0)/2 in J/m^3, hence for E = 0 the field energy density u = B^2/(2 mu0); the magnetic stress is T_ij = (1/mu0)(delta_ij B^2/2 - B_i B_j) (tension B^2/2mu0 along B, pressure B^2/2mu0 across it).
published_hypotheses: classical (non-quantised) Maxwell theory: linear vacuum electrodynamics, no vacuum polarisation -- valid for B << B_c = m_e^2 c^2/(e hbar) = 4.414e9 T (computed here from CODATA 2022)
vacuum (mu = mu0); in a linear medium the field energy is B.H/2, not B^2/2mu0
SI units with x^0 = ct; u is the 00 component of the stress-energy tensor -- the energy density measured by a static observer -- NOT a null contraction T_kk
flat background (or local inertial frame); minimal coupling
hypothesis_drift: ADDED -- u identified with T_kk. spec.py:156 (seating_invariant = sqrt(2 mu0 T_COEFF), i.e. B^2/2mu0 := T_kk), spec.py:271-276 (WITHDRAWN 2 compares u_far to seatindex.tkk_required), spec.py:303-304 (consistency check energy_density(1e11) vs tkk_required(1.5456e8)); seatindex.py:209-211 defines the threshold on T_kk. Machine-checked here (part B): for E = 0 and null k = (1,n), T_kk = (B^2/mu0) sin^2(theta) = 2u sin^2(theta), ranging over [0, 2u]; it equals u only at sin^2(theta) = 1/2. The source's u is T_00, not T_kk. Same identification in charge.py:145-152 (magnetic_energy_density fed to seats_beyond), not a listed owner.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS OK (exit 0, ~3 s). (A) Hilbert stress tensor from the SI Maxwell action by differentiating sqrt(-g)L w.r.t. g^ab: T_00 = (eps0 E^2 + B^2/mu0)/2 exactly; E=0 gives B^2/(2 mu0) = spec.py:178-179; trace zero. (B) E=0, null k=(1,n): T_kk = 2u sin^2(theta), NOT u. (C) tree invariant 1.54562e19 T m reproduced; with T_kk = 2u (B across path) it would be 1.09292e19 (factor 1/sqrt2). WITHDRAWN 2: u-as-T_kk gives 7.34e-26 (25.13 orders short); T_kk = 2u gives 1.47e-25 (24.83 orders); T_kk = 0 along the axis -- the withdrawal holds under every orientation. Seat/collapse with T_kk = 2u would be pi^2/3 = 3.29 instead of 2pi^2/3 = 6.58, still > 1 (context only; WITHDRAWN 1 is posed for generic u). (D) one-loop EH (Schwinger proper-time representation, NAMED-NOT-READ, integrand validated only to reproduce its own weak-field -alpha b^2/45pi): du/u = -9.57e-4 at 1e11 T; approaches -(alpha/3pi)(ln b - 2.29) at large b (checked b = 1e4..1e8); far field -1.9e-27.

later_literature.what: Quantum vacuum polarisation makes B^2/2mu0 the leading term of u = -L_eff(B); the correction is O(alpha b^2) below B_c and logarithmic above it. Computed here numerically: -9.57e-4 at 1e11 T. Narrows the formula's validity to B << B_c at the 1e-3 level; does not move any tree conclusion.

lacked_data: What classical electrodynamics lacked: (1) quantum vacuum polarisation (Heisenberg-Euler 1936) and any observed field near B_c = 4.414e9 T -- magnetar-class fields (~1e11 T) are the exact regime the tree evaluates at spec.py:304. Having that data changes u by -9.57e-4 at 1e11 T (computed), inside the tree's 1e-3 tolerance, and by -1.9e-27 at the far field where WITHDRAWN 2 is decided; no conclusion moves. (2) The post-2019 SI makes mu_0 measured rather than exact; the tree already uses the measured CODATA 2018 value, and the 2022 update moves u by 6.8e-10. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the classical formula is exact within its stated hypotheses and follows from the action (machine-checked). Evidence for a narrowing: it is a vacuum, classical, T_00 statement -- the substantive gap is not missing data but the tree's identification of T_00 with T_kk (factor 2 sin^2(theta)), which is a use-site drift, not a defect of the external result.
grade_evidence: The external formula u = B^2/(2 mu0) is re-derived exactly from the SI Maxwell action (sympy, part A) and the mu_0 move (2018->2022, 6.8e-10) moves nothing -- as a statement it stands. It is graded NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than it holds: (i) the tree treats u as the null contraction T_kk (spec.py:156, 271-276, 303-304; seatindex.py:209-211), while for a pure magnetic field T_kk = 2u sin^2(theta) in [0, 2u] (machine-checked, part B); (ii) the tree drops B << B_c and evaluates at 1e11 T = 22.7 B_c, where one-loop QED shifts u by -9.57e-4 (computed, part D). NEITHER MOVES A TREE CONCLUSION: WITHDRAWN 2 stays > 24.8 orders short under every orientation (and infinitely short along the axis); the withdrawn B*l invariant would read 1.09292e19 rather than 1.54562e19 T m if B lay across the path -- a numerical discrepancy in an already-withdrawn figure, recorded not repaired; the spec.py:303-304 consistency check passes with or without the EH shift. Caveat carried: the source was NOT read at source (alphaXiv quota, arxiv 403) -- the grade rests on the in-environment derivation from the Maxwell action and on CODATA read from scipy's bundled NIST table.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restricting its use to T_00 (or writing T_kk = 2u sin^2(theta) with the path orientation declared) and stating B << B_c (or carrying the EH correction) where it evaluates at magnetar fields. To OPEN-flagged re-audit: a read at source (Jackson/L&L restatement on arXiv, Dunne hep-th/0406216, CODATA 2409.03787) that disagreed with the sympy derivation -- not expected, but the read has not happened. Nothing on record would make it WRONG: no counterexample to the formula within its hypotheses exists here.
